Try itP alone: why the AV stays 0.42 m/s short
Goal: find where P alone stops changing.
  • holding a speed needs throttle \(=\) drag / 4
  • P gives \(0.5 \times e\)
  • speeds chosen for this example:

Click a row (or press Enter on it): a popup explains its numbers.

speed \(v\) (m/s)drag \(= 0.15 + 0.012\,v^2\)needed \(=\) drag / 4error \(e\)P \(= 0.5\,e\)the AV
8.00\(0.15 + 0.77 = 0.92\)0.2300slows down
7.80\(0.15 + 0.73 = 0.88\)0.220.200.10slows down
7.58\(0.15 + 0.69 = 0.84\)0.210.420.21holds
7.40\(0.15 + 0.66 = 0.81\)0.200.600.30speeds up
7.00\(0.15 + 0.59 = 0.74\)0.181.000.50speeds up

Above 7.58 m/s, P gives less than drag needs and the AV slows; below, more, and it speeds up.

The issueP makes throttle only from an error, and the AV needs throttle to hold any speed, so P must keep an error: 0.42 m/s short for good. Fix: add I, which pushes with no error.
